Emilia — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire PDF. Opening notes below, and we attached a short answers pack that maps to each SecuraHealth question (airlocked-deploy-capabilities-answers.pdf). Highlights first: 

1) Egress controls: Redwood Private supports strict egress whitelisting at the network layer and an optional policy-enforced outbound proxy. Customers can provide a list of allowed FQDNs/IPs or export tokens to an internal mirror. For fully airgapped installs we support an operator-controlled egress gateway appliance that requires manual approval to push bundles out.

2) KMS/HSM integration: We have an HSM integration shim that supports PKCS#11 and KMIP. Keys may be stored in-customer HSM — the runtime can be configured to perform crypto ops via remote HSM calls; private key material is never persisted on the inference hosts. We will attach the KMS/HSM integration notes (kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf).

3) Patch/update process: For airgapped customers we provide signed update bundles that are delivered via a secure transfer method (SFTP or USB, operator choice). Each bundle is signed with Redwood's release key and includes a checksum and SBOM. Operators validate signature and run the pre-checks in the operator-runbook-condensed.md; staging can be performed in an isolated test VLAN before promotion.

Attachments: airlocked-deploy-capabilities-answers.pdf (summary), kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf, network-diagram-v2.png, operator-runbook-condensed.md

Next step: Laura and Rishi — looping you for any technical gaps. We can also host a 45-min lab walkthrough with your security team and TPI next week. Proposed slots: Wed 6/9 10:00 or Thu 6/10 14:00 PT.

Cheers,

Emilia — answering your follow-ups below (consolidated for the packet). Where appropriate I call out the reference material pages in the attached PDF.

- HSM network flow: For customer-managed HSMs the inference hosts initiate outbound TLS connections to the HSM management endpoint (PKCS#11 over TLS or KMIP). Typical deployment is an internal-only routed network where the inference nodes have TCP 443 egress to the HSM cluster VIP. Optionally, customers may deploy a dedicated crypto-proxy in the same VLAN to mediate calls; this proxy is operated by the customer and placed behind the egress ACLs. (See kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf §2)

- Bundle signing: SecuraHealth can bring its own signing key. Our signed-bundle process supports dual-signing: Redwood signs to attest build provenance and the customer may add an external signature before promotion. The operator-runbook contains the commands to validate both signatures prior to install (operator-runbook-condensed.md, step 4).

- Operator pre-promotion checks (automatable):
  * Verify bundle signature(s) and checksum (sha256)
  * Compare SBOM against approved component list
  * Run smoke-start in isolated test node and validate KV cache recovery
  * Confirm network CIS rules: outbound allowed IPs and DNS overrides present
  * Execute service-level healthcheck that exercises model load and tokenization path

- Data retention attestation: We can provide a single-page signed attestation stating that when configured with customer retention=0 and KMS-backed ephemeral keys, the runtime does not persist model inputs or derived embeddings. Attached as a signed PDF in the Drive link.

Attachments (in this thread): airlocked-deploy-capabilities-answers.pdf, kms-hsm-integration-notes.pdf, network-diagram-v2.png, operator-runbook-condensed.md

Links for your packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-secure-airlock-evidence (contains attestation PDF and signed-bundle sample)
